subject: Vendor replacement — risk-adjusted pricing and onboarding fees

Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement lead asked me to get a clearer view of the economic differences if we move from our current vendor to Redwood. Two specific asks:

- A risk-adjusted credit schedule for the first 6 months (we want to account for integration/latency regressions).
- A breakdown of one-time onboarding fees vs ongoing commit discounts — specifically whether pilot credits can be applied to committed capacity.

Can you share a concise worksheet or a quick example pack that shows how you typically structure a deal for customers with a phased pilot (3 months) followed by a committed tier? Also would appreciate any common caveats around egress or hidden fees.

We may need legal to see a draft term showing liability/rollback protection if the integration doesn't meet SLAs.

Best,
Ethan

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching two artifacts: a short onboarding runbook with a sample fixed-fee estimate and a small CSV with Q2 benchmark deltas we typically observe for similar customers. High-level answers inline below and we can walk through in a 30-minute call if helpful.

1) Risk-adjusted credits: We typically offer a staged credit schedule tied to go-live milestones and SLA gates. Example: 30% pilot credit applied to invoice during pilot; 20% onboarding credit upon data migration completion; an additional run-rate credit (spread over first three billing cycles) if latency or correctness regressions exceed thresholds. Credits are separate from commit discounts and are intended to offset onboarding risk.

2) Pilot credits vs commit discounts: Pilot credits are one-time offsets and do not reduce committed unit pricing. For customers that convert to a committed tier within 90 days, we can apply a portion of the unused pilot credit towards the first committed invoice, up to a defined cap (usually 50% of pilot credit). Commit discounts are priced by committed token/embedding volumes and start the month the commit begins.

3) One-time onboarding fees: These cover data transfer, custom connector work, and runbook-assisted migration. We prefer to keep these explicit rather than bake into unit pricing; they can be credited back against the initial invoices under a conversion event as above.

4) Egress/hidden fees: Redwood charges egress only when data exits a customer's VPC or goes to an unaffiliated cloud region. Most typical integrations have negligible egress if customers keep inference calls within our managed environment. We'll flag any non-standard flows in the runbook.

I looped in Jonas (commercial) and Lauren (onboarding) to confirm the numbers. If you want, Jonas can propose a two-option commercial anchor (conservative and aggressive) and Lauren can outline a trimmed onboarding runbook.

Would you be available Wed 06 Oct for a 30m sync?

Thanks,
Sofia

Jonas / Lauren — forwarding SwitchGrid note. Quick priorities:

- Provide two commercial anchors: (A) conservative: small pilot credit + standard commit discount; (B) conversion-friendly: larger pilot credit + partial apply to first invoice if they convert within 60–90 days. Keep total economic cost neutral over 12 months.
- Quantify onboarding one-time fee in line items (data egress estimate, connector dev, runbook-hours). Lauren — can you draft a trimmed runbook with a hard-dollar estimate and a best/worst case for hours?
- Include a short escalation/rollback clause they can show to legal: e.g., SLA breach > X days triggers a credit equal to Y% of monthly invoice. Match typical market phrasing without opening full warranty risk.

Target to send a consolidated commercial note + attachments to Ethan by EOD Monday (05 Oct). I will own the commercial anchor.

Thanks,
Sofia

Subject: RE: exploring replacement options — need clarity on credits and onboarding fees

Ethan — thanks for the patience. Attaching a short commercial memo and the onboarding runbook Lauren prepared (summary below). I pulled two anchor options as Sofia requested.

Anchor A (Conservative)
- Pilot: 25% credit applied to pilot invoice (3-month duration)
- Onboarding fee: $18,000 (data migration + two connector sprints + 24 runbook hours)
- Commit discount: 10% off list for 12-month commit starting month after pilot
- SLA rollback: credit equal to 15% of the impacted month if latency/regression thresholds exceeded for >7 days

Anchor B (Conversion-friendly)
- Pilot: 40% credit applied to pilot invoice
- Onboarding fee: $12,000 if commit confirmed within 60 days (we absorb part of connector effort into conversion credit)
- Commit discount: 12% off list for 12-month commit
- SLA rollback: credit equal to 10% of the impacted month if thresholds exceeded for >7 days

Notes:
- We can apply up to 50% of unused pilot credit to the first committed invoice in Anchor B.
- Estimated egress: negligible for their planned architecture (see benchmarks_q2.csv).

If this looks reasonable, happy to convert Anchor B into a short sideletter draft for legal review.

Best,
Jonas

Attachments referenced: runbook_onboarding_estimate.pdf, benchmarks_q2.csv
